techniques.name: Activate Firmware Update Mode
techniques.summary: Adversaries may activate firmware update mode on devices to prevent expected response functions from engaging in reaction to an emergency or process malfunction.

techniques.name: Monitor Process State
techniques.summary: Adversaries may gather information about the physical process state.

techniques.name: Automated Collection
techniques.summary: Adversaries may automate collection of industrial environment information using tools or scripts.

techniques.name: Brute Force I/O
techniques.summary: Adversaries may repetitively or successively change I/O point values to perform an action.

techniques.name: Command-Line Interface
techniques.summary: Adversaries may utilize command-line interfaces (CLIs) to interact with systems and execute commands.

techniques.name: Data Destruction
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform data destruction over the course of an operation.

techniques.name: Data from Information Repositories
techniques.summary: Adversaries may target and collect data from information repositories.

techniques.name: Denial of Control
techniques.summary: Adversaries may cause a denial of control to temporarily prevent operators and engineers from interacting with process controls.

techniques.name: Denial of Service
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks to disrupt expected device functionality.

techniques.name: Denial of View
techniques.summary: Adversaries may cause a denial of view in attempt to disrupt and prevent operator oversight on the status of an ICS environment.

techniques.name: Device Restart/Shutdown
techniques.summary: Adversaries may forcibly restart or shutdown a device in an ICS environment to disrupt and potentially negatively impact physical processes.

techniques.name: Drive-by Compromise
techniques.summary: Adversaries may gain access to a system during a drive-by compromise, when a user visits a website as part of a regular browsing session.

techniques.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
techniques.summary: Adversaries may leverage weaknesses to exploit internet-facing software for initial access into an industrial network.

techniques.name: Exploitation for Evasion
techniques.summary: Adversaries may exploit a software vulnerability to take advantage of a programming error in a program, service, or within the operating system software or kernel itself to evade detection.

techniques.name: Modify Controller Tasking
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify the tasking of a controller to allow for the execution of their own programs.

techniques.name: External Remote Services
techniques.summary: Adversaries may leverage external remote services as a point of initial access into your network.

techniques.name: Graphical User Interface
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to gain access to a machine via a Graphical User Interface (GUI) to enhance execution capabilities.

techniques.name: Loss of Availability
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to disrupt essential components or systems to prevent owner and operator from delivering products or services.

techniques.name: Loss of Control
techniques.summary: Adversaries may seek to achieve a sustained loss of control or a runaway condition in which operators cannot issue any commands even if the malicious interference has subsided.

techniques.name: Loss of Productivity and Revenue
techniques.summary: Adversaries may cause loss of productivity and revenue through disruption and even damage to the availability and integrity of control system operations, devices, and related processes.

techniques.name: Loss of View
techniques.summary: Adversaries may cause a sustained or permanent loss of view where the ICS equipment will require local, hands-on operator intervention; for instance, a restart or manual operation.

techniques.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
techniques.summary: Adversaries with privileged network access may seek to modify network traffic in real time using adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) attacks.

techniques.name: Manipulation of Control
techniques.summary: Adversaries may manipulate physical process control within the industrial environment.

techniques.name: Manipulation of View
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to manipulate the information reported back to operators or controllers.

techniques.name: Native API
techniques.summary: Adversaries may directly interact with the native OS application programming interface (API) to access system functions.

techniques.name: Manipulate I/O Image
techniques.summary: Adversaries may manipulate the I/O image of PLCs through various means to prevent them from functioning as expected.

techniques.name: Modify Parameter
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify parameters used to instruct industrial control system devices.

techniques.name: Loss of Protection
techniques.summary: Adversaries may compromise protective system functions designed to prevent the effects of faults and abnormal conditions.

techniques.name: Modify Alarm Settings
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify alarm settings to prevent alerts that may inform operators of their presence or to prevent responses to dangerous and unintended scenarios.

techniques.name: Network Connection Enumeration
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform network connection enumeration to discover information about device communication patterns.

techniques.name: Network Sniffing
techniques.summary: Network sniffing is the practice of using a network interface on a computer system to monitor or capture information regardless of whether it is the specified destination for the information.

techniques.name: Program Download
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform a program download to transfer a user program to a controller.

techniques.name: Download All
techniques.summary: Adversaries may execute a full program download to a PLC to overwrite the entire PLC program and configuration to deploy a new project or make major changes.

techniques.name: Online Edit
techniques.summary: Adversaries may execute an online edit of a PLC to update parts of an existing program.

techniques.name: Program Append
techniques.summary: Adversaries may execute a program append to a PLC to update parts of an existing program.

techniques.name: Program Upload
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to upload a program from a PLC to gather information about an industrial process.

techniques.name: Remote System Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of other systems by IP address, hostname, or other logical identifier on a network that may be used for subsequent Lateral Movement or Discovery techniques.

techniques.name: Port Scan
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform a port scan on a system, device, or network to identify live hosts, enumerate open ports and running services, identify operating systems, and map out the network.

techniques.name: Broadcast Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform broadcast discovery requests to enumerate systems and devices on a network.

techniques.name: Multicast Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform multicast discovery requests which is when one system or device sends messages to all systems and devices in a pre-defined group on a network (or subnet) and then waits for a response.

techniques.name: Replication Through Removable Media
techniques.summary: Adversaries may move onto systems, such as those separated from the enterprise network, by copying malware to removable media which is inserted into the control systems environment.

techniques.name: Rogue Master
techniques.summary: Adversaries may setup a rogue master to leverage control server functions to communicate with outstations.

techniques.name: Masquerading
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use masquerading to disguise a malicious application or executable as another file, to avoid operator and engineer suspicion.

techniques.name: Rootkit
techniques.summary: Adversaries may deploy rootkits to hide the presence of programs, files, network connections, services, drivers, and other system components.

techniques.name: Screen Capture
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to perform screen capture of devices in the control system environment.

techniques.name: Scripting
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use scripting languages to execute arbitrary code in the form of a pre-written script or in the form of user-supplied code to an interpreter.

techniques.name: Change Operating Mode
techniques.summary: Adversaries may change the operating mode of a controller to gain additional access to engineering functions such as Program Download.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.summary: Adversaries may steal the credentials of a specific user or service account using credential access techniques.

techniques.name: Wireless Compromise
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform wireless compromise as a method of gaining communications and unauthorized access to a wireless network.

techniques.name: Point & Tag Identification
techniques.summary: Adversaries may collect point and tag values to gain a more comprehensive understanding of the process environment.

techniques.name: Supply Chain Compromise
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform supply chain compromise to gain control systems environment access by means of infected products, software, and workflows.

techniques.name: User Execution
techniques.summary: Adversaries may rely on a targeted organizations user interaction for the execution of malicious code.

techniques.name: Transient Cyber Asset
techniques.summary: Adversaries may target devices that are transient across ICS networks and external networks.

techniques.name: Spearphishing Attachment
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use a spearphishing attachment, a variant of spearphishing, as a form of a social engineering attack against specific targets.

techniques.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
techniques.summary: Adversaries may exploit a software vulnerability to take advantage of a programming error in a program, service, or within the operating system software or kernel itself to enable remote service abuse.

techniques.name: Lateral Tool Transfer
techniques.summary: Adversaries may transfer tools or other files from one system to another to stage adversary tools or other files over the course of an operation.

techniques.name: Detect Operating Mode
techniques.summary: Adversaries may gather information about a PLCs or controllers current operating mode.

techniques.name: Standard Application Layer Protocol
techniques.summary: Adversaries may establish command and control capabilities over commonly used application layer protocols such as HTTP(S), OPC, RDP, telnet, DNP3, and modbus.

techniques.name: Execution through API
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to leverage Application Program Interfaces (APIs) used for communication between control software and the hardware.

techniques.name: Indicator Removal on Host
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to remove indicators of their presence on a system in an effort to cover their tracks.

techniques.name: Project File Infection
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to infect project files with malicious code.

techniques.name: Siemens Project File Format
techniques.summary: Adversaries may infect Siemens PLC project files (i.e., Step 7, WinCC, etc.) to achieve [Execution](https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0104), [Persistence](https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0110), and [Lateral Movement](https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0109) objectives.

techniques.name: Hooking
techniques.summary: Adversaries may hook into application programming interface (API) functions used by processes to redirect calls for execution and privilege escalation means.

techniques.name: I/O Image
techniques.summary: Adversaries may seek to capture process values related to the inputs and outputs of a PLC.

techniques.name: Alarm Suppression
techniques.summary: Adversaries may target protection function alarms to prevent them from notifying operators of critical conditions.

techniques.name: Damage to Property
techniques.summary: Adversaries may cause damage and destruction of property to infrastructure, equipment, and the surrounding environment when attacking control systems.

techniques.name: Loss of Safety
techniques.summary: Adversaries may compromise safety system functions designed to maintain safe operation of a process when unacceptable or dangerous conditions occur.

techniques.name: Service Stop
techniques.summary: Adversaries may stop or disable services on a system to render those services unavailable to legitimate users.

techniques.name: Theft of Operational Information
techniques.summary: Adversaries may steal operational information on a production environment as a direct mission outcome for personal gain or to inform future operations.

techniques.name: Internet Accessible Device
techniques.summary: Adversaries may gain access into industrial environments through systems exposed directly to the internet for remote access rather than through [External Remote Services](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T0822).

techniques.name: Connection Proxy
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use a connection proxy to direct network traffic between systems or act as an intermediary for network communications.

techniques.name: Commonly Used Port
techniques.summary: Adversaries may communicate over a commonly used port to bypass firewalls or network detection systems and to blend in with normal network activity, to avoid more detailed inspection.

techniques.name: Remote Services
techniques.summary: Adversaries may leverage remote services to move between assets and network segments.

techniques.name: Wireless Sniffing
techniques.summary: Adversaries may seek to capture radio frequency (RF) communication used for remote control and reporting in distributed environments.

techniques.name: Remote System Information Discovery
techniques.summary: An adversary may attempt to get detailed information about remote systems and their peripherals, such as make/model, role, and configuration.

techniques.name: Modify Program
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify or add a program on a controller to affect how it interacts with the physical process, peripheral devices and other hosts on the network.

techniques.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
techniques.summary: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities in an attempt to elevate privileges.

techniques.name: Change Credential
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify software and device credentials to prevent operator and responder access.

techniques.name: Data from Local System
techniques.summary: Adversaries may target and collect data from local system sources, such as file systems, configuration files, or local databases.

techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution
techniques.summary: Adversaries may bypass process and/or signature-based defenses by proxying execution of malicious content with signed, or otherwise trusted, binaries.

techniques.name: Autorun Image
techniques.summary: Adversaries may leverage AutoRun functionality or scripts to execute malicious code.

techniques.name: Block Operational Technology Message
techniques.summary: Adversaries may block messages between systems and devices in an OT/ICS environment to disrupt processes.

techniques.name: Command Message
techniques.summary: Adversaries may block a command message from reaching its intended target to prevent command execution.

techniques.name: Reporting Message
techniques.summary: Adversaries may block or prevent a reporting message from reaching its intended target.

techniques.name: Unauthorized Message
techniques.summary: Adversaries may send unauthorized messages to ICS systems and devices to evade defenses or manipulate processes.

techniques.name: Command Message
techniques.summary: Adversaries may send unauthorized command messages to instruct control system assets to perform actions outside of their intended functionality, or without the logical preconditions to trigger their expected function.

techniques.name: Reporting Message
techniques.summary: Adversaries may spoof reporting messages in control system environments for evasion and to impair process control.

techniques.name: Modify Firmware
techniques.summary: Firmware is low-level software embedded in hardware that enables systems and devices to function properly and is commonly found in ICS environments.

techniques.name: System Firmware
techniques.summary: System firmware on modern assets is often designed with an update feature.

techniques.name: Module Firmware
techniques.summary: Adversaries may install malicious or vulnerable firmware onto modular hardware devices.

techniques.name: Insecure Credentials
techniques.summary: Adversaries may target insecure credentials as a means to persist on a system or device or move laterally from one system or device to another.

techniques.name: Default Credentials
techniques.summary: Adversaries may leverage manufacturer or supplier set default credentials on control system devices.

techniques.name: Hardcoded Credentials
techniques.summary: Adversaries may leverage credentials that are hardcoded in software or firmware to gain an unauthorized interactive user session to an asset.

techniques.name: Block Communications
techniques.summary: Operational technology communications occur over serial COM, Ethernet, Wi-Fi, cellular (4G/5G), and satellite mediums.

techniques.name: Serial COM
techniques.summary: Adversaries may block access to serial COM to prevent instructions or configurations from reaching target devices.

techniques.name: Ethernet
techniques.summary: Adversaries may block access to Ethernet communications to prevent instructions or configurations messages from reaching target systems and devices.

techniques.name: Wi-Fi
techniques.summary: Adversaries may block access to Wi-Fi communications to prevent messages from reaching target systems and devices.
